subject: physics
question_text: At the same temperature and pressure, compare the rms speed of oxygen molecules with that of hydrogen molecules. (Molar mass of O₂ = 32, H₂ = 2 g/mol)

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 13 Short Answer Question 5 (printed p.140). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The four-way mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: v_rms = √(3RT/M) gives v ∝ 1/√M at fixed T; with M(O₂) = 32 and M(H₂) = 2, v(O₂)/v(H₂) = √(2/32) = √(1/16) = 1/4, so the ratio is 1 : 4, matching the brief's independently checked arithmetic.

steps.label: Formula and proportionality
lines: v_rms = √(3RT/M) for a gas of molar
steps.margin_note: First mark. Write the formula, then the proportionality it gives at fixed T.
steps.why: The rms speed formula shows M in the denominator inside a square root, so the temperature and gas constant cancel when the two gases are compared at the same T.
common_mistakes: Using the molar masses of atomic O and H, 16 and 1, instead of the molecules O₂ and H₂, 32 and 2.
Forgetting the square root and taking the ratio of the masses directly.
steps.memory_tip: Heavier gas, slower molecules: v_rms goes as 1 over root M.

steps.label: Molar masses
lines: Molar mass of oxygen, M(O₂) = 32 g/mol.
Molar mass of hydrogen, M(H₂) = 2 g/mol.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Both molar masses must be named before the ratio is set up.
steps.why: The ratio needs both molar masses in the same unit; grams per mole is what the periodic table gives directly.
common_mistakes: Using the atomic mass of one hydrogen atom, 1, instead of the diatomic molecule H₂, 2.
steps.memory_tip: O₂ is sixteen times heavier than H₂: 32 against 2.

steps.label: Setting up the ratio
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Set up the ratio with the lighter gas's mass on top.
steps.why: Because v_rms ∝ 1/√M the mass ratio inverts, so for v(O₂)/v(H₂) the lighter gas's molar mass, M(H₂) = 2, goes in the numerator.
common_mistakes: Inverting the ratio and writing √(M(O₂)/M(H₂)), which gives 4 instead of 1/4.
Writing 2/32 as 1/16 without showing the substitution step.
steps.memory_tip: The gas named FIRST in the ratio pairs with the OTHER gas's mass on top.

steps.label: Final ratio
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. State the final ratio, in the right order, with both gases named.
steps.why: Oxygen molecules are 16 times heavier, so their rms speed is only √16 = 4 times smaller than hydrogen's.
common_mistakes: Writing the answer as 4:1 without checking which gas is faster.
Leaving the answer as a fraction, 1/4, instead of stating it as a ratio.
steps.memory_tip: Oxygen is heavier, so it is the slower one: oxygen to hydrogen is 1 to 4.

insider_note: The ratio must be stated the right way round — oxygen to hydrogen is 1:4, not 4:1. Say which gas each number belongs to.
